entries.canonical_text: "Takehiro, a kind samurai, married my daughter Masago,"
entries.primary_text: Takahiro, a kind samurai, married my daughter Masako.
entries.secondary_text: Takehiro, a kind samurai, married my daughter Masago.

entries.canonical_text: Masago said at the temple. "The bandit had left him tied up. I begged him to die with me. His cold eyes said I was nothing, even though I was his wife. "He moved his lips while I held my dagger. 'Kill me,' he said, so I stabbed him. I could not stand those eyes.
entries.primary_text: Masago sat at the temple. The bandit had left him tied up. I begged him to die with me. His cold eyes said I was nothing, even though I was his wife. He moved his lips while I held my dagger. Kill me, he said. So I stabbed him. I could not stand those eyes.
entries.secondary_text: Masago said at the temple. The bandit had left him tied up. I begged him to die with me. His cold eyes said I was nothing, even though I was his wife. He moved his lips while I held my dagger. Kill me, he said. So I stabbed him. I could not stand those eyes.

entries.canonical_text: Takehiro's spirit said through a medium. "She asked him to take her anywhere. Then she pointed at me: 'Kill that man.' "He pushed her away and asked if she should live or die. I nearly forgave him then, but she ran away. He cut one rope and left me. "I got up beside the cedar and picked up her small dagger. She had dropped it there. I pushed it into my own chest. "The bushes around me grew quiet. Someone came slowly towards me on silent feet. A hand I could not see quietly pulled the dagger from my chest.
entries.primary_text: Takahiro's spirit said through a medium. She asked him to take her anywhere. Then she pointed at me. Kill that man. He pushed her away and asked if she should live or die.
